file.content: Can symbolic verification via a provably sound solver improve Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning when constraints are self-extracted from the model's own traces? Despite Z3 validating 99\% of such constraints, the answer is no. We introduce Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts logical constraints from chain-of-thought traces and selects answers via weighted MAX-SAT, yet produces answers identical to Self-Consistency (SC) majority voting on 94.4\% of problems. Across six models (7B--32B), three reasoning domains, and over 3{,}000 condition-evaluations, no condition shows a significant positive effect after FDR control; four conditions confirm equivalence within $\pm$2\,pp, while ten remain underpowered for effects below ${\sim}$2\,pp. We trace this failure to \emph{symbolic confirmation bias}: on incorrect problems, 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong majority answer, with bias ratios from $1.66\times$ to $4.97\times$ across nine models from 7B to frontier scale. A shuffle control confirms this bias is structural ($p > 0.7$) and extends the self-correction impossibility of \citet{huang2024selfcorrect} to formal verification. All twenty-seven training-free remediation strategies fail due to a persistent independence-accuracy trade-off. Preliminary evidence suggests that structurally independent cross-architecture NLI verification can escape the bias ($+6.67$\,pp on the weakest generator, $p < 0.001$). Three zero-cost diagnostics ($K_\text{eff}$, BR, $C_0$) correctly classify all 60 tested conditions and allow practitioners to predict a priori whether symbolic aggregation will help.

3	\label{sec:conclusion}
4	
5	\looseness=-1
6	The three diagnostics ($K_\text{eff}$, BR, $C_0$) extend beyond SICA to any trace-aggregation method, correctly classifying all 60 tested conditions. Decision boundaries generalize prospectively to a held-out model family (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic-framework}), enabling practitioners to predict viability from a pilot run ($K{=}12$) at zero cost. The framework provides actionable guidance: before deploying any symbolic aggregation pipeline, run $K{=}12$ traces, compute the three metrics, and check against the decision boundaries. This avoids the $4.5\times$ computational overhead of methods that will not improve over majority voting.
7	
8	\looseness=-1
9	With $K_\text{eff} \leq 3.6$ for $K{=}12$ across instruction-tuned models, same-model traces scale redundancy, not information. This has direct consequences for test-time compute scaling \citep{snell2025scaling}: generating more traces from the same model yields diminishing returns bounded by the effective independence ceiling. Effective scaling requires either structurally independent verifiers (\S\ref{sec:cross-arch}) or trained signals that escape the model's distributional prior \citep{cobbe2021gsm8k, lightman2024prm}. The monotonic capability-gap relationship (\S\ref{sec:cross-arch}) further implies that as generators improve, the bar for useful verification rises correspondingly.
10	
11	\looseness=-1
12	Symbolic confirmation bias applies to any method extracting structured representations from LLM traces. Self-verification \citep{weng2023selfverification}, self-refinement \citep{madaan2023selfrefine}, and chain-of-verification \citep{dhuliawala2023chainofverification} all face the same distributional prior when the verification signal originates from the same model. Formal soundness of the verifier is necessary but not sufficient; extraction must be independent. This distinguishes our finding from prior work on self-correction limitations \citep{huang2024selfcorrect}: we show that even provably correct formal solvers become vacuous when the input constraints inherit the model's bias.
13	
14	\looseness=-1
15	Escaping the bottleneck requires three conditions: (i)~\emph{structural independence}, where the verifier shares neither architecture nor training data with the generator; (ii)~\emph{capability ordering}, where the verifier exceeds the generator's accuracy on the target domain; and (iii)~\emph{task-verifier alignment}. Whether trained extractors or multi-modal verification can shift the independence-accuracy trade-off boundary remains open. Extending the diagnostic framework to non-logical reasoning domains and evaluating self-extraction on frontier models with internal tool access are natural next steps.

file.content:
\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
\label{sec:discussion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

\looseness=-1
The three diagnostics ($K_\text{eff}$, BR, $C_0$) extend beyond SICA to any trace-aggregation method, correctly classifying all 60 tested conditions. Decision boundaries generalize prospectively to a held-out model family (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic-framework}), enabling practitioners to predict viability from a pilot run ($K{=}12$) at zero cost. The framework provides actionable guidance: before deploying any symbolic aggregation pipeline, run $K{=}12$ traces, compute the three metrics, and check against the decision boundaries. This avoids the $4.5\times$ computational overhead of methods that will not improve over majority voting.

\looseness=-1
With $K_\text{eff} \leq 3.6$ for $K{=}12$ across instruction-tuned models, same-model traces scale redundancy, not information. This has direct consequences for test-time compute scaling \citep{snell2025scaling}: generating more traces from the same model yields diminishing returns bounded by the effective independence ceiling. Effective scaling requires either structurally independent verifiers (\S\ref{sec:cross-arch}) or trained signals that escape the model's distributional prior \citep{cobbe2021gsm8k, lightman2024prm}. The monotonic capability-gap relationship (\S\ref{sec:cross-arch}) further implies that as generators improve, the bar for useful verification rises correspondingly.

\looseness=-1
Symbolic confirmation bias applies to any method extracting structured representations from LLM traces. Self-verification \citep{weng2023selfverification}, self-refinement \citep{madaan2023selfrefine}, and chain-of-verification \citep{dhuliawala2023chainofverification} all face the same distributional prior when the verification signal originates from the same model. Formal soundness of the verifier is necessary but not sufficient; extraction must be independent. This distinguishes our finding from prior work on self-correction limitations \citep{huang2024selfcorrect}: we show that even provably correct formal solvers become vacuous when the input constraints inherit the model's bias.

\looseness=-1
Escaping the bottleneck requires three conditions: (i)~\emph{structural independence}, where the verifier shares neither architecture nor training data with the generator; (ii)~\emph{capability ordering}, where the verifier exceeds the generator's accuracy on the target domain; and (iii)~\emph{task-verifier alignment}. Whether trained extractors or multi-modal verification can shift the independence-accuracy trade-off boundary remains open. Extending the diagnostic framework to non-logical reasoning domains and evaluating self-extraction on frontier models with internal tool access are natural next steps.

All datasets are English-language logical reasoning benchmarks; we do not evaluate trained symbolic extractors, multilingual settings, or commonsense domains lacking gold annotations. \section{Results}
\label{sec:results}
\label{sec:main-results}

\looseness=-1 Table~\ref{tab:main_results} reports accuracy across all non-degenerate self-extraction conditions sorted by SC baseline. No condition shows a significant SICA effect after FDR control (BH, $m{=}16$). Two conditions show nominally significant degradation: Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($-2.83$\,pp, raw $p = 0.014$) and Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter ($-2.50$\,pp, raw $p = 0.011$); both reach adjusted $p = 0.112$. An aggregate sign test yields 8 positive and 7 negative $\Delta$ values ($p = 1.00$, two-sided).

\begin{table*}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{SICA vs.\ SC across all non-degenerate self-extraction conditions (sorted by SC). No condition shows a significant gain after BH correction ($m{=}16$). $\Delta$ = SICA $-$ SC (pp). Symbols: $^b$gold ICL; \textbf{bold}: $p < 0.05$; {*}\,uncorrected $p < 0.05$ (BH adj.\ $p = 0.112$); $^{3s}$\,3-seed; $^{4s}$\,4-seed confirmatory (unmarked: single-seed exploratory). Degenerate conditions ($C_0 < 5\%$: QwQ-32B AIME, Qwen2.5-14B GSM8K) yield $\Delta = 0$; oracle upper bounds are reported in Appendix~\ref{app:oracle}.}
\label{tab:main_results}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llrrrrl@{}}
\toprule
Model & Domain & $n$ & SC (\%) & SICA (\%) & $\Delta$ (pp) & $p$ \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type C: error amplification (SC $\leq$ 40\%)}} \\
Mistral-7B & PW-D5 & 600 & 39.33 & 36.50 & $\mathbf{-2.83}$ & 0.014{*} \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Intermediate SC (SC $\sim$50--60\%, Mistral-7B only)}} \\
Mistral-7B & LogiQA & 200 & 50.00 & 51.50 & $+$1.50 & 0.581 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s123) & 204 & 54.41 & 57.35 & $+$2.94 & 0.070 \\
Mistral-7B$^{3s}$ & FOLIO & 204 & 56.53 & 56.70 & $+$0.16 & 1.000 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s456) & 204 & 55.88 & 55.88 & 0.00 & 1.000 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s789) & 204 & 59.31 & 56.86 & $-$2.45 & 0.267 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type A: confirmation bias (SC $\geq$ 60\%)}} \\
LLaMA-3.1-8B & FOLIO & 204 & 66.18 & 61.76 & $-$4.41 & 0.093 \\
LLaMA-3.1-8B & StrategyQA & 200 & 72.00 & 74.00 & $+$2.00 & 0.424 \\
\addlinespace
Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO (ICL)$^b$ & 199 & 74.37 & 74.87 & $+$0.50 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-14B & PW-D5 & 600 & 74.00 & 71.50 & $\mathbf{-2.50}$ & 0.011{*} \\
Qwen2.5-14B$^{4s}$ & FOLIO & 204 & 75.98 & 75.49 & $-$0.49 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-7B & FOLIO & 204 & 75.98 & 76.47 & $+$0.49 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-14B & LogiQA & 200 & 79.00 & 78.00 & $-$1.00 & 0.625 \\
\addlinespace
Qwen3-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 83.33 & 84.80 & $+$1.47 & 1.000 \\
Qwen3-14B & PW-D5 & 600 & 85.83 & 85.67 & $-$0.17 & 1.000 \\
Qwen3-14B (think) & FOLIO & 204 & 86.27 & 86.76 & $+$0.49 & 1.000 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table*}

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{f2_regime_scatter}
\caption{SICA $\Delta$ (pp) vs.\ SC baseline. Filled: $n \geq 100$; open: $n < 100$. The intermediate-SC region (50--60\%, shaded) contains the only positive trends (none reaching $p < 0.05$). Type~C: nominally significant degradation (raw $p = 0.014$; BH adj.\ $p = 0.112$).}
\label{fig:regime-scatter}
\end{figure}

\looseness=-1 Figure~\ref{fig:regime-scatter} reveals the regime structure underlying these results. Fleiss' $\kappa$ ranges from 0.21 to 0.82 across conditions, yielding $K_{\text{eff}} = 1.20\text{--}3.62$ at $K = 12$ (Table~\ref{tab:independence}, Appendix). Positive $\Delta$ requires both sufficient $K_{\text{eff}}$ ($\leq 1.30$ never improves) and reasonable SC accuracy ($K_{\text{eff}} = 3.62$ with SC $= 39\%$ degrades rather than helps). Three regimes emerge: Type~C (SC $\leq 40\%$), where low base accuracy causes error amplification; an intermediate band (50--60\%), containing the only positive trends; and Type~A (SC $\geq 60\%$), where symbolic confirmation bias dominates. Seed-level noise is substantial: across four Mistral-7B seeds, $\kappa \in [0.41, 0.51]$ yet $\Delta$ ranges from $+3.43$ to $-0.49$\,pp, indicating that constraint quality varies beyond what independence alone predicts. We trace the failure mechanism in \S\ref{sec:analysis}.

\looseness=-1 TOST equivalence tests \citep{lakens2017equivalence} with margin $\pm 2$\,pp confirm four conditions as equivalent; ten remain underpowered for effects below ${\sim}2$\,pp (MDE 1.86--4.84\,pp; Appendix~\ref{app:power}). Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence for small effects. Three-seed replication on Mistral-7B confirms seed-level noise (mean $\Delta = +0.16 \pm 2.70$\,pp; Table~\ref{tab:multi-seed}). Four-seed replication on Qwen2.5-14B $\times$ FOLIO confirms the pattern ($\Delta \in [0.00, -2.01]$\,pp).

\looseness=-1 Oracle controls replacing self-extracted constraints with gold annotations confirm the MAX-SAT mechanism is sound ($+29.90$/$+13.73$\,pp FOLIO, $+17.17$\,pp ProofWriter; $p < 0.001$), yet self-extraction captures only ${\sim}$12\% of this ceiling (Appendix~\ref{app:oracle}).
